subject: MSA + Order Form: mapping liability caps to SLA credit remedies
messages:
From: Amir Khan <amir.khan@acme-analytics.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft MSA / Order Form — liability + SLA credits

Hannah,

Thanks for sending the draft. Our GC reviewed the liability section and came back with two asks we need to reconcile before we proceed to procurement:

1) Carve-outs for data-related claims: they want an explicit exclusion for liability arising from our downstream data processing where Acme is the data controller; language like "claims arising from Customer's processing of Customer Data using the Service" excluded from the Vendor cap.

2) Sole remedy + credits: they are OK with service credits as a remedy for availability incidents but want an explicit path to damages if credits are insufficient — specifically, a clause permitting claims for direct damages above the credit cap when certain thresholds of recurring SLA breaches occur.

Can you confirm Redwood's position? Also attaching the redline from our side.

Attachments: Acme_redline_MSA_v2.docx (docx)

Regards,
Amir Khan
Sr. Contracts Manager
Acme Analytics
From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
To: Amir Khan <amir.khan@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft MSA / Order Form — liability + SLA credits

Amir — thanks, and appreciated the quick review. Looping in Dev (sales) and Lauren (legal ops) to weigh in. High level:

- Data carve-out: Redwood's standard position is to exclude certain controller-side claims tied to customer-controlled data processing, but we need precise language so it doesn't swallow core service liability.
- Sole remedy: we normally include service credits as the sole and exclusive remedy for SLA failures, with a carve allowing direct damages up to the monetary cap for other breaches. We resist an unlimited pathway from repeated credits to full damages, but will consider narrowly-tailored exceptions (e.g., repeated severe breaches documented in the SLA reporting window).

Requesting Dev to propose concrete redline language that balances Acme's ask with our risk limits. Lauren — can you ensure the proposed language is operationally testable (so it's not an open-ended escrow to damages)?

Hannah Schmitt
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
From: dev_patel@redwood.ai
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, Amir Khan <amir.khan@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 13:40:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed redline: mapping credits to cap / limited exception

Amir / team — thanks for the note. I put together a short redline proposal and attached a worked example spreadsheet showing how recurring SLA breaches would map to credit payouts vs. the monetary cap. Summary of our proposal (see Proposed_MSA_redlines_v3.docx):

- Maintain standard limitation of liability: aggregate cap equals 12 months' subscription fees for the Order Form.
- Preserve that service credits are the exclusive remedy for SLA availability incidents up to the credit cap defined in the SLA schedule.
- Carve a narrow exception: if (i) the same SLA objective is missed in 4 consecutive monthly measurement windows OR (ii) the annualized total uncredited downtime exceeds 20% of billed SLA hours, then Customer may recover direct damages exceeding the credit amount but still subject to the aggregate monetary cap. This exception requires documented SLA reports and a 30-day cure window before damages are recoverable.

Rationale: gives Acme an escape hatch for persistent outages while keeping our aggregate exposure bounded and giving ops time to remediate. Please see SLA_credit_calcs.xlsx for examples. Happy to iterate.

Regards,
Dev Patel
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Proposed_MSA_redlines_v3.docx (docx), SLA_credit_calcs.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@acme-analytics.com>
To: dev_patel@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: Amir Khan <amir.khan@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposed redline: mapping credits to cap / limited exception

Thanks Dev — the worked example helped. A few follow-ups from legal and procurement:

- They want the carve for controller-led processing to be explicit and limited to third-party processing claims (i.e., not supplier negligence that causes customer data loss). Suggested wording: "Claims arising solely from Customer's processing decisions or Customer-owned third-party integrations shall not reduce Vendor's liability cap, provided such claims do not arise from Vendor's gross negligence or willful misconduct."

- The exception threshold (4 consecutive months) seems reasonable, but procurement asks that the 30-day cure window start from the date the Customer provides the signed SLA report rather than from our internal detection. They also want an option to escalate to a C-level review if the exception is triggered.

- Finally, on enforceability: they asked whether Redwood will accept a commitment to preserve logs/audit reports for 24 months to support any later damages claim.

Can you confirm acceptance on these operational points so we can circulate a consolidated redline back to GC?

—Sofia
Director, Procurement
Acme Analytics
From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
To: Amir Khan <amir.khan@acme-analytics.com>, Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 15:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposed redline: mapping credits to cap / limited exception — next steps

Amir / Sofia — thanks for the concrete feedback. Quick confirmation on our side:

1) Data carve-out: we can accept the narrow controller-processing carve-out you proposed, with explicit carve-back for Vendor's gross negligence or willful misconduct. Lauren will embed final wording in the doc.

2) Cure window & reporting: we accept the 30-day cure window triggered by Customer-provided signed SLA report. Ops will commit to preserving audit traces for 24 months to support any escalation; I'll copy the SRE lead on the final draft.

3) C-level review: acceptable — we will insert an escalation path to a joint executive review if the exception is triggered.

4) Exception mechanics: we prefer to keep the aggregate cap (12 months' fees) unchanged; any damages above monthly credits remain subject to that cap.

Next steps: Lauren to update Proposed_MSA_redlines_v3.docx with the agreed language and return a consolidated redline by EOD Monday. Dev and I will prep a short exec summary for the renewal committee if Acme requests it.

Hannah Schmitt
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
